paragraphs: The HomePod operating system occasionally needs updating, because the device is a lot more than a simple speaker — it’s a computer. Here’s how to make sure your Apple smart speaker has the software version released on Friday. You’ll want it even though the new HomePod Software version 27.2.1 is just bug fixes.
If you depend on automatic updates, it’s likely your smart speaker hasn’t yet installed the update. Here’s how to do so manually.

Apple offers macOS, iOS and several other platforms. You might think the operating system for HomePod would have a similar name. Internally, Apple employees call it audioOS, but the company never uses that name publicly. For everyone else, it’s simply “HomePod Software.”

It’s apparently a variation of Apple TV’s tvOS that’s been specially modified for the smart speaker. This makes sense — both focus on multimedia playback, support Siri, and don’t need to worry about cellular-wireless connections.
New HomePod Software versions come out when Apple updates the Apple TV software. And the version numbers are generally in lockstep. With tvOS 27.2.1 out now, it’s also time for a HomePod update.

To be current, your Apple smart speaker should be on HomePod Software Version 27.2.1. This is true whether you own an original HomePod, HomePod 2, HomePod mini or HomePod mini 2. The previous version, 27.2, came out in October.

That 27.2 update ushered in many new features, including a new Sound Glow visual experience when playing music, home theater surround sound support and the option to make a HomePod the audio output for everything on a Mac with a persistent AirPlay connection.
After a few weeks of use, that last version apparently needs tweaking. Apple’s release note for version 27.2.1 says, “This update provides bug fixes.”
